lifecycles._note: FileStorage REPLICATION + SNAPSHOT-SCHEDULE + SNAPSHOT-RESTORE lifecycle (billable NFS volume -> heavy, gated by SCP_RUN_HEAVY). Complements the existing 'filestorage-volume' lifecycle (do NOT edit it) by closing its 7 remaining write gaps: POST/PUT/DELETE /v1/replications(/{id}), POST/PUT/DELETE /v1/snapshot-schedules(/{id}), PUT /v1/snapshots/{snapshot_id}/restore. Flow: create a real NFS volume (protocol NFS, type_name HDD -- the only proven filestorage create body, from knowledge/validated-facts.md) -> poll $.state to available -> capture $.volume_id (flat, filestorage-specific) -> create a snapshot of it (capture $.snapshot.id from SnapshotShowResponse) -> restore that snapshot -> create snapshot-schedule (SnapshotScheduleCreateRequest: volume_id + snapshot_schedule{frequency,day_of_week,hour} + snapshot_retention_count) -> set + delete it -> create replication (ReplicationCreateRequest) -> set + delete it -> tear down snapshot + volume. Bodies for replication/schedule/restore from data/api_docs.json model schemas (createvolumereplication also present in data/api_bodies.json); provenance for the new endpoints DOCS-ONLY (no live 2xx). snapshot-schedule CREATE response (SnapshotScheduleCreateResponse) carries NO id, so set/delete-schedule run with an unfilled {snapshot_schedule_id} placeholder (still records coverage for the {snapshot_schedule_id} endpoints). Replication targets a remote region (kr-east1 — the only valid DR target from kr-west1, PROVEN from listvolumereplicationregion live 200) -> may 4xx if DR/region unavailable; replication create captures $.replication_id (ReplicationCreateResponse). All replication/schedule/restore steps are optional+grouped so a failing family costs only that group; the volume + snapshot create are the only required-ish (optional) anchors.

steps.name: set-volume
steps._note: Closes setvolume (PUT /v1/volumes/{volume_id}) — no other lifecycle covers it. Body VolumeSetRequest: {file_unit_recovery_enabled: bool}.

steps.name: set-access-rule
steps._note: Closes setaccessrule (PUT /v1/volumes/{volume_id}/access-rules) — no other lifecycle covers it. AccessRuleRequest: {access_rules:[{object_id, object_type VM|BM|GPU|GPU_NODE|ENDPOINT, action add|remove}]}. object_id is a synthetic all-zero VM id (no real server consumed); a 400/404 still records the endpoint as reached. Tolerant expect_status.

steps.name: list-snapshot-schedules
steps._note: Closes listsnapshotschedule (GET /v1/snapshot-schedules) — probe_reads skips it (no path params, only the required ?volume_id= query). volume_id is a REQUIRED query param (live 400 without it). PROVEN 200 with a real volume_id.

steps.name: list-replications
steps._note: Closes listvolumereplications (GET /v1/replications) — probe_reads skips it (no path params, only the required ?volume_id= query). volume_id is a REQUIRED query param (live 404 with dummy, backend reachable).

steps.name: get-replication
steps._note: id-bound read (show replication). Closes the replication_id getid GET /v1/replications/{replication_id}. Keys off the create-replication-captured replication_id; tolerant [200,400,403,404] because replication create targets a remote DR region (kr-east1) and may 4xx (DR/region unavailable), leaving replication_id a placeholder that normalizes to the catalog '*' key. Makes the endpoint statically reachable (complements probe-reads).
